name: Basalt Sea Stacks
desc: Columnar basalt sea stacks standing off a cold coast in fog — four planes of rock dissolve into the haar one behind the other, each drifting at its own rate, banks of sea fog scroll between them and swallow the far ones whole, and the swell works white around their feet; North Atlantic large-format, a wet-collodion dry plate, flat woodblock planes, an x-ray lattice of the jointing, or a graphite study.

energy.doc: how hard the sea works the rock — swell amplitude, foam wash, and overall contrast

scale.doc: how monumental the stacks are — height and column width (rebuilds the planes)

density.doc: how many stacks per plane, how many swell lines and wash points

fog.doc: aerial perspective — how completely the far planes dissolve into the haar

swell.doc: sea state, from oily calm to a running swell

hue.doc: palette hue shift off the default cold grey-green

x.doc: which way the light rakes across the rock faces

y.doc: horizon height — high y gives more water, low y towers the stacks

style.doc: aesthetic: haar = cold North Atlantic large-format with modelled rock; dryplate = warm wet-collodion, blown highlights, plate flaws; ukiyo = flat woodblock tonal planes, hard edges, no interior modelling; xray = transparent wireframe lattice of the columnar jointing, no mass; graphite = colourless pencil study, tone built only from hatching

act.doc: multi-minute weather programme — fog lifting, fog closing in, or a gale running

seed.doc: regenerates the stacks, their jointing and the fog banks

alpha.doc: how far the world sits back behind the performers
